extracted.intended_audience: electronic journalists and newsroom staff (radio, television, digital news)
extracted.subtask_description: Collection/landing page listing RTDNA professional standards: the organization's Code of Ethics and a set of coverage guidelines for electronic journalism. Topics cover specific reporting situations (breaking news, privacy, juveniles, graphic content), technical issues (audio/video editing, digital manipulation), and legal/First Amendment concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: RTDNA Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: The RTDNA Code of Ethics was revised in 2015 and can now be found at http://www.rtdna.org/content/rtdna_code_of_ethics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization-level ethics code for electronic journalists; primary authoritative statement of ethical standards for members — follow the full linked code for detailed principles and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Guidelines (umbrella)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage Guidelines Info — a collection of topic-specific guidance on how to cover difficult or sensitive reporting situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an index to many specific guidance documents (see individual topics below) that outline standards, practices, and cautions for news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for covering breaking news events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards and cautions for rapid coverage situations; see linked guide for balancing speed with accuracy and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on on-the-scene live reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses verification, context, reporter safety, and ethical live broadcasting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone Calls On‑Air
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance about broadcasting telephone calls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers consent, disclosure, recording notices, verification and legal/ethical considerations before airing phone content.

rubrics_metrics.name: 911 Calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on use of 911 emergency calls in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider privacy, editing, and safety implications; follow legal restrictions and ethical standards to avoid harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bomb Threats
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for reporting on bomb threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers safety, verification, preventing panic, and coordination with authorities before broadcasting threat details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shooting / Hostage Situation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for coverage of shootings and hostage events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes verifying information, avoiding speculation, protecting victims' privacy, and not interfering with emergency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law Enforcement Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reporting police and law-enforcement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers access, verification, use of scanner information, relations with authorities, and balance between public interest and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Police Scanners
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance about relying on police scanner traffic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns about verification, context, potential for inaccurate or incomplete information, and considerations about publicizing tactical information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bioterrorism Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for reporting on bioterrorism or related threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses accuracy, public safety, avoiding unnecessary alarm, and use of expert sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and standards to prevent plagiarism in journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices for attribution, sourcing, original reporting, and consequences/handling of plagiarism incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respecting Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on respecting individuals' privacy in news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework for when to publish private information, balancing public interest and harm, and handling sensitive personal details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the use and protection of confidential sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers promises of anonymity, verification requirements, legal protections and limits, and newsroom policies for handling confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to evaluate credibility and reliability of sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for vetting sources, cross-checking, corroboration, and distinguishing between eyewitness, official, and anonymous sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden Cameras
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance about the use of hidden cameras in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses ethical justification, legality, consent, minimization of harm, and editorial standards for when covert recording is permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Tape
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using archived audio/video ('file tape') in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for proper labeling, date/context disclosure, and avoiding misleading reuse of old material as current.

rubrics_metrics.name: User‑Generated Content (UGC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using material created by the public (photos, video, social posts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses verification, consent, attribution, legal clearance, and assessing authenticity and context of UGC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on handling graphic images or descriptions (violence, gore).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for viewer warnings, necessity vs. sensationalism, editing to minimize harm, and considering audience sensibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying Juveniles
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when and how to identify minors in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes protecting juveniles' privacy and safety, legal limits, and ethical considerations before naming or showing minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing Juveniles
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for interviewing children and teenagers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on consent, parental involvement, appropriate questioning, avoiding harm, and special verification practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racial Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when to include racial or ethnic identification in reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles for relevance, avoiding stereotyping, and minimizing gratuitous or biased identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Suicide
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to responsibly report suicides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes avoidance of sensational language/details, providing resources, suicide-prevention best practices, and minimizing contagion risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video / Audio Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on ethical standards for editing audio and video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers not changing meaning, avoiding deceptive splices, indicating edits where necessary, and maintaining accuracy and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on altering digital images, audio or video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits misleading manipulation; requires disclosure of significant alterations and strict standards to preserve authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Editorial Audio and Video
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance distinguishing editorial content from non-editorial audio/video (ads, promos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for labeling, separation from news coverage, and avoiding blurring of advertising and editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amber Alerts
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on broadcasting Amber Alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices for disseminating alerts quickly while ensuring accuracy and coordination with authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charitable Solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when and how news organizations handle charitable appeals or solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies for accepting/promoting solicitations, disclosure, avoiding conflicts of interest, and preserving newsroom independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media and Blogging
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on journalists' use of social media platforms and blogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers personal vs. professional accounts, verification of social media content, standards for engagement, and avoiding conflicts or bias online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism Values
rubrics_metrics.description: General guidance on core journalism values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad principles such as accuracy, fairness, independence, accountability, and serving the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death and Dying
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for reporting on death, terminal illness, and dying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on sensitivity, family privacy, verification, and avoiding gratuitous detail or sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on covering funerals and memorials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cultural sensitivity, family wishes, privacy, and appropriateness of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on identifying and managing conflicts of interest in journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies about financial, personal or organizational relationships that could compromise or appear to compromise impartial reporting; disclosure and recusal practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance relating to promotional content by news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish promotional material from editorial content; avoid using news platform to unduly promote unrelated entities without disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on sponsored content that mimics editorial (native ads).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear labeling, separation from editorial voice, and transparency to avoid misleading audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cameras in the Courts Guide (state and federal variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on courtroom camera policies, including state-specific guides (AL‑ID, IL‑MN, MS‑NC, ND‑TN, TX‑WY) and Federal Courts guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides legal/regulatory information and best practices for televising or recording court proceedings; includes state-by-state differences and federal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment News / FOIA News
rubrics_metrics.description: Category/guidance on First Amendment issues and freedom-of-information (FOIA) news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers legal updates, case law, FOIA practice, and implications for news gathering and access to public records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Vest Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentioned as a First Amendment/legal news topic (likely guidance related to reporters' access or identification in certain situations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to linked legal/advocacy materials for specific interpretation and newsroom implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunshine Week
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to public-information/transparency advocacy (Sunshine Week).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages reporting practices that promote government transparency and public access to records; see resources for events and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need legal advice? (resource prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt/heading offering legal advice resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates RTDNA provides or links to legal assistance/resources for journalists — not a standard itself but a pointer to legal support.
